name: windows_batch
description: Execute click/type/fill/wait/snapshot actions in order, returning numbered results and structured step outcomes. Stops on errors by default; always stops when an action is still pending. Never replay a pending action.

handle.description: Window handle for snapshot or input

actions.description: The steps to run in order, at most 100: each an action and its arguments.

stopOnError.description: Stop executing if an action fails (default: true)

name: windows_click
description: Click an element by its ref (from windows_snapshot). Prefers Invoke pattern for reliability (tree and list rows: select), falls back to mouse click if needed. Menu items and controls whose name ends in "..." get a physical click by default, because an Invoke that opens a menu or dialog blocks UI Automation until it closes; pass physical=false to force Invoke. If the click opens a modal dialog, returns immediately with the dialog title instead of waiting for the dialog to close. A select fallback click reports whether SelectionItem confirms selection; an unconfirmed click must be inspected before continuing. A right-click after selecting a tree or list row can start inline rename; open context menus with windows_send_keys Shift+F10 or Apps.

handle.description: Optional window handle; when supplied, the ref must belong to this window.

physical.description: Use a physical mouse click with foreground and native-window hit checks. Defaults to true for menu items and names ending in "...", otherwise false. These checks do not prove which UIA child receives the click; a container's clickable point may hit a child control.

action.description: Pattern to use instead of the default choice. Tree and list rows default to select, because Invoke on a tree row toggles its expansion; expand/collapse open or close a tree node without selecting it; click forces a mouse click.

name: windows_close
description: Close a window.

name: windows_fill
description: Clear and fill a text field with new value. Prefers Value pattern for reliability; a value set that way reads back through the same pattern, so the call is unverified (not Filled) until you observe the control. A field in a common file dialog is filled by keyboard instead. Without a writable Value pattern it focuses the control and sends Ctrl+A, then Backspace or the new text; it refuses before any key when the control does not take keyboard focus. Reports Filled only when the control reads the value back independently.

handle.description: Optional window handle to validate against the element ref.

verifyFocus.description: Keyboard fallback only: require verified keyboard focus before Ctrl+A, true for the exact control, "self-or-descendant" for it or any descendant. By default the exact control, or its Edit child when the ref is a ComboBox or Spinner, or a focused Edit inside it with no other value control in between; set false only for a control that never reports focus, and the keys then go wherever focus is.

name: windows_find
description: Find controls with exact UIA selectors (nameContains for a partial name) and optional ancestor scope (within, e.g. a pane's TitleBar to tell identical Close buttons apart; ancestry:true shows each match's parents); returns compact properties, patterns and fresh refs. Omit selector for bounded raw-tree inspection. An absent state field means unknown. Does not invalidate snapshot refs.

handle.description: Window identifier from windows_list_windows or windows_launch (e.g. w1) to search in.

selector.description: What to match; every field given must match. Omit it for a bounded walk of the raw tree.

nameContains.description: Case-insensitive substring of name. Use it when you know only part of a label.

rootOnly.description: Match only the search root, not descendants.

controlType.description: UIA type, e.g. Button, Edit, Tree, MenuItem

text.description: Matches name OR value. Prefer it when you know what a control shows on screen: grid, tree and list rows usually carry a positional name such as 'Node0' or 'Name row 87' with the label in value.

within.description: An ancestor to search under, such as a pane's TitleBar to tell identical buttons apart.

nameContains.description: Case-insensitive substring of name. Use it when you know only part of a label.

rootOnly.description: Match only the search root, not descendants.

controlType.description: UIA type, e.g. Button, Edit, Tree, MenuItem

text.description: Matches name OR value. Prefer it when you know what a control shows on screen: grid, tree and list rows usually carry a positional name such as 'Node0' or 'Name row 87' with the label in value.

includeOwned.description: Also search other visible native windows of this process, including popup menus (unscoped only).

maxDepth.description: How many levels below the search root to descend (default 24).

maxNodes.description: Client-side traversal/result budget; cannot interrupt a blocking provider query.

ancestry.description: Show each match's parents, to tell identical matches apart.

includeBounds.description: Include physical screen bounds; omitted by default.

name: windows_focus
description: Bring a window to the foreground and give it focus.

handle.description: Window handle from windows_list_windows or windows_launch

name: windows_get_clipboard
description: Read the Windows clipboard's text. Mainly for controls that expose no text to UI Automation, such as Scintilla editors: focus one, select all, copy, then read it here. While an app allowlist is active the text must have been put there by an allowed app, since the clipboard is shared with every other application.

name: windows_get_text
description: Get an element's accessible text. Prefer its Text or Value pattern for content, then fall back to selection, legacy value, or Name. Password content is unavailable.

name: windows_launch
description: Launch a Windows application. Returns a window handle for use with other tools.

app.description: Path to executable or UWP app ID (e.g., 'calc.exe', 'notepad.exe', 'C:\\Program Files\\MyApp\\app.exe')

waitSeconds.description: Poll for a unique window from this process for up to this many seconds after startup (1-90; default 20). Cold starts such as TE3 can need 45 or more; allow a longer caller timeout.

name: windows_list_windows
description: List all open windows with their handles, titles, and process names. Use this to find windows to interact with.

name: windows_mouse
description: Move the pointer or click a captured window point. park: move it off the window so no tooltip or hover state lands in a screenshot. move/hover: to a point or ref. scroll: wheel ticks over a point or ref (positive scrolls up). click: left- or right-click at a point or ref (`button` defaults to left). drag: press at `from` (or ref, or ref's fromEdge), move in steps, release at `to`, toRef/toEdge, or wherever resizeTo makes ref that size (a column header: ref + fromEdge right + resizeTo 250). Use it for splitters and other targets UI Automation does not expose. Points are pixels in a windows_screenshot of the same window (handle), so read them straight off a capture.

action.description: park, move, hover, scroll, drag or click; see the tool description for what each needs.

handle.description: Window handle; points are relative to its capture.

ref.description: Element to move to, hover, scroll over, or drag from.

from.description: Drag start in window pixels (alternative to ref).

to.description: Target in window pixels: move/hover/scroll/click point, or drag end.

ticks.description: scroll: wheel ticks, positive is up.

fromEdge.description: drag: grab this edge of ref instead of its centre (e.g. right for a column header's divider).

fromMustHit.description: drag with a raw from point: refuse before input unless the point is on this element ref.

toMustHit.description: drag with a raw to point: require this element ref before input and recheck it before release.

toRef.description: drag: release on this element instead of a `to` point.

fromMustNotHit.description: drag: refs the start point must not land on (a neighbouring pane's caption, say); the drag is refused before the button goes down when UI Automation reports one of them, or something inside it, there.

toEdge.description: drag: which part of toRef to release on (default center; left drops a column header before it).

resizeTo.description: drag with ref + fromEdge: release where ref becomes this many pixels wide (left/right) or tall (top/bottom). One call, no screenshot needed.

name: windows_operation_status
description: Read-only status for running, timed-out, and completed operations. status is ok or failed once finished (running or timed_out_pending before); dispatch says how much input went out: completed, partial, not-dispatched, timed_out_pending (still running; never replay) or unknown, with inputsSent. provider is pending while a click it started still blocks UI Automation on that app (usually an open menu or dialog). No UI Automation calls.

operationId.description: An operationId from a tool's structuredContent; omit it for every retained operation.

name: windows_paste
description: Paste text into an element by ref, or the focused element, with the clipboard and Ctrl+V. Use it for code and multi-line text, which code editors autocomplete when typed. Overwrites the clipboard; the app may still reformat what it receives.

handle.description: Optional explicit window handle; otherwise uses the focused element.

ref.description: Element ref from windows_snapshot or windows_find. If omitted, pastes into the focused element.

verifyFocus.description: Require ref and verified keyboard focus on that exact control before pasting (default false). Worth setting for code editors: an unverified paste inserts text wherever focus happens to be.

name: windows_place_window
description: Move or resize an observed normal-state native window in physical screen pixels without activating it. Returns requested and observed bounds; the operating system may constrain size. Rejects clipping and child controls; never replays the move.

ref.description: A top-level window ref; alternative to handle.

handle.description: Window identifier from windows_list_windows (for example w1), not a numeric HWND; alternative to ref.

placement.description: The bounds to request, in physical screen pixels.

name: windows_screenshot
description: Capture a window, element or the screen as PNG. Normal capture uses UIA bounds and may omit the title bar; strictNative captures the whole native window. With savePath and includeImage=false only the path is returned; view the saved image before claiming a visual result.

frame.description: Optional exact source-size assertion and pixel crop; no rescaling.

handle.description: Window handle. If omitted, captures the foreground window.

fullScreen.description: Capture the entire screen (default: false). Disabled while an app allowlist is active.

background.description: Native whole-window capture. A handle falls back to screen pixels; a Window ref does not. Not with fullScreen.

strictNative.description: Native whole-window capture with no screen-pixel fallback. Needs a handle or Window ref.

savePath.description: Absolute local .png file path to save the screenshot. UNC and device paths are rejected.

overwrite.description: Allow savePath to replace an existing file (default: false)

includeImage.description: Return image payload (default true). Set false with savePath for compact artifact-only output.

includeMetadata.description: Append capture method, bounds, crop, size and DPI.

locate.description: Element refs whose rectangles to measure in the returned image, reported as {ref, x, y, width, height, clipped} in image pixels. Use this instead of converting windows_find bounds yourself: those are screen coordinates from an earlier observation, they go stale when the layout moves, and the offset between the two is not constant across DPI states. Implies includeMetadata. Refused when the capture cannot be trusted to map 1:1.

parkPointer.description: Move the pointer off the window first, so no tooltip or hover highlight lands in the image (default false). Use it for any capture that will be published.

allowOccludedPixels.description: Capture screen pixels even when another application's window covers part of the target (default false). Only for deliberately capturing a partly covered window: the image will contain whatever is on top. strictNative is usually the better answer, since it renders the window's own surface and is unaffected by what is in front of it.

name: windows_send_keys
description: Send key presses or key chords to an element by ref or the focused element. Supports either `chord` (single chord, e.g., Ctrl+Right) or `keys` array (sequence, e.g., ["Ctrl+C","Ctrl+V"]).

handle.description: Optional explicit window handle; otherwise uses the focused element.

verifyFocus.description: Require verified keyboard focus before the sequence: true for the ref's exact control, "self-or-descendant" for it or a descendant (an editable ComboBox focuses its Edit child), false for no check. Default "self-or-descendant" when a ref is given, since keys such as Ctrl+A or Delete go wherever focus is.

expectFocusClass.description: Abort without sending unless the focused control's window class matches this exactly, rechecked before every chord. Use it for ref-less or handle-only input, which is otherwise unverified: the keys go wherever focus happens to be. Every reply names the focused class, so run once to discover it.

ref.description: Element ref from windows_snapshot (e.g., 'w1e5'). If omitted, sends to focused element.

chord.description: Single key chord string, e.g. 'Ctrl+Right' or 'Alt+F4'.

name: windows_set_window_state
description: Maximize, restore (normal) or minimize a top-level window. Use restore before windows_place_window, which only moves normal-state windows. Returns the state and bounds observed afterwards; one attempt, never replayed.

ref.description: Alternative to handle: a top-level window ref.

state.description: maximize, minimize, or restore (normal is the same as restore).

name: windows_snapshot
description: Capture accessibility snapshot of a window. Returns a structured tree with element refs that can be used with windows_click, windows_type, etc. Prefer windows_find for known selectors and compact state; use this to explore unfamiliar structure. A new snapshot invalidates earlier refs for that window.

handle.description: Window handle from windows_launch or windows_list_windows. If omitted, uses the foreground window.

maxNodes.description: Client-side node budget (default 3000); cannot interrupt a blocking provider call.

maxCharacters.description: Output character budget including partial-result notice (default 20000).

name: windows_type
description: Type text into an element. The element will be focused first. Line breaks are sent as Enter. Code editors can autocomplete typed text; use windows_paste for code. Use this for typing without clearing existing content. Use windows_fill to replace content.

handle.description: Optional explicit window handle; otherwise uses the focused element.

verifyFocus.description: Require ref and verified keyboard focus on that exact control before typing (default false).

ref.description: Element ref from windows_snapshot (e.g., 'w1e5'). If omitted, types to currently focused element.

name: windows_wait
description: Wait for scoped UIA presence, settled absence, or one control's value/selected/toggle state. Does not send input. Incomplete searches cannot prove absence; rootOnly excludes descendants.

handle.description: Window identifier from windows_list_windows or windows_launch (e.g. w1) to watch.

selector.description: The control to wait for; every field given must match.

nameContains.description: Case-insensitive substring of name. Use it when you know only part of a label.

rootOnly.description: Match only the search root, not descendants.

controlType.description: UIA type, e.g. Button, Edit, Tree, MenuItem

text.description: Matches name OR value. Prefer it when you know what a control shows on screen: grid, tree and list rows usually carry a positional name such as 'Node0' or 'Name row 87' with the label in value.

nameContains.description: Case-insensitive substring of name. Use it when you know only part of a label.

rootOnly.description: Match only the search root, not descendants.

controlType.description: UIA type, e.g. Button, Edit, Tree, MenuItem

text.description: Matches name OR value. Prefer it when you know what a control shows on screen: grid, tree and list rows usually carry a positional name such as 'Node0' or 'Name row 87' with the label in value.

includeOwned.description: Also search other visible native windows of this process, including popup menus.

state.description: present or absent (absence must hold for settleMs), or the matched control's value, selected or toggle state equal to expected.

expected.description: String for value/toggle (On, Off, Indeterminate), boolean for selected.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait before giving up, in milliseconds (default 5000).

settleMs.description: How long absence must hold before it counts, in milliseconds (default 500).

maxNodes.description: Client-side node budget for each search (default 3000); an incomplete search cannot prove absence.
